MARTA KOWAL-BRANDT
Cloud Infrastructure / DevOps Engineer
Wroclaw, Poland | marta.kowalbrandt@example.com | +48 555 303 303 | gitlab.com/mkb-example

PROFESSIONAL SUMMARY
QA automation engineer with 7 years of experience, including hands-on work building CI/CD pipelines, Kubernetes-based ephemeral environments, and developer tooling for three product teams. Brings practical infrastructure-as-code experience from a personal Terraform project, alongside Docker, Helm, Linux, and monitoring experience. Known for taking ownership of shared engineering workflows and documenting them for team onboarding. Moving toward a full-time DevOps / platform engineering role.

TECHNICAL SKILLS
Infrastructure & CI/CD: Terraform (personal project), GitLab CI, Jenkins, Docker, Docker Compose, Helm, Argo CD
Containers & Linux: Kubernetes (namespace-level experience), k3s, Linux
Monitoring & data: Prometheus, Grafana, Loki, PostgreSQL
Networking & security: Traefik ingress, cert-manager TLS
Languages & tools: Python, Bash, Java (test code), SQL, Git, Ansible (basic)
Cloud learning: AWS EC2 and S3 basics; Hetzner VPS
Testing: pytest, Playwright, Selenium, Postman

PROFESSIONAL EXPERIENCE

QA Automation Engineer (Test Infrastructure) | Odrava Health Software, Wroclaw | 2021–Present
- Own GitLab CI pipelines for three product teams (~25 developers), covering build, unit, integration and end-to-end test stages, and artifact publishing.
- Reduced average pipeline duration from 38 to 14 minutes by profiling workflows, parallelising test jobs, adding dependency caching, and separating end-to-end tests into their own stage; monthly CI runner costs fell by about 30%.
- Built short-lived merge-request environments for applications, PostgreSQL and seeded data, deploying with Helm to the shared Kubernetes cluster from GitLab CI. Environments are automatically removed after merge or 48 hours of inactivity.
- Maintain a pytest and Playwright end-to-end suite of about 900 tests; reduced the flaky-test rate from 7% to below 1%.
- Wrote Bash and Python tooling to seed PostgreSQL test data and built a Python/GitLab API workflow that collected CI test results into PostgreSQL for Grafana dashboards.
- Wrote the internal guide to how CI works, which is used in team onboarding; mentored two QA interns in 2023.
- Work with namespace-level access on the shared Kubernetes cluster; the platform team operates the cluster.

QA Engineer | Brightmill Software House, Wroclaw | 2019–2021
- Tested web and mobile applications for client projects through manual and automated testing.
- Introduced a Java and Selenium automated regression suite for the largest client project.
- Configured Jenkins jobs to run nightly regression tests.

Customer Support Specialist (2nd line) | Brightmill Software House | 2018–2019
- Investigated customer issues using logs and databases, and reproduced bugs for developers.

SELECTED INFRASTRUCTURE PROJECTS

Homelab k3s Cluster with GitOps | Personal | 2024–2025
- Built a three-node k3s cluster on Raspberry Pi 5 devices and deployed applications from a Git repository using Argo CD.
- Set up Prometheus, Grafana and Loki for monitoring, Traefik ingress and cert-manager for TLS.
- Provisioned infrastructure for a small Hetzner VPS with Terraform; used Ansible at a basic level.

Merge-Request Ephemeral Environments | Odrava Health | 2023–2024
- Developed an automated workflow to deploy a short-lived application and PostgreSQL environment, with seeded data, for each merge request.
- Integrated deployments and end-to-end testing with GitLab CI; environments are automatically removed after merge or 48 hours of inactivity.

CI Pipeline Speed-up | Odrava Health | 2022
- Profiled pipelines across three teams, parallelised test jobs, added dependency caching and separated end-to-end tests into their own stage.
- Reduced average pipeline duration from 38 to 14 minutes and monthly CI runner costs by about 30%.

EDUCATION
BEng Computer Engineering | Silesian Lowlands University of Technology | 2018

CERTIFICATIONS & PROFESSIONAL DEVELOPMENT
ISTQB Foundation Level | 2019
Certified Kubernetes Administrator (CKA) preparation; exam scheduled for January 2027

LANGUAGES
Polish (native) | English (C1) | German (A2)

critique.content_quality_feedback: This is a strong, well-structured and professional CV with clear progression from QA automation toward DevOps/platform engineering. The strongest content is the quantified impact: pipeline duration reduced from 38 to 14 minutes, runner costs reduced by approximately 30%, and flaky tests reduced from 7% to below 1%. The CV also gives useful scope indicators, including three product teams and approximately 25 developers. The infrastructure projects add relevant evidence beyond the candidate's formal QA title. The main content limitation is that some bullets describe tools and activities without explicitly connecting them to architecture, stakeholder coordination, security, or operational outcomes relevant to this particular role. The repeated coverage of the same ephemeral-environment and pipeline-speed work in both Experience and Selected Infrastructure Projects also uses space that could be used for stronger role alignment.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: The document is ATS-friendly overall: it uses standard section headings, conventional reverse chronology, plain-text contact details, and recognizable keyword groupings. Relevant terms such as Terraform, GitLab CI, Kubernetes, Helm, Docker, Linux, AWS, TLS, Prometheus, Grafana, and PostgreSQL are present. The title and summary are also directionally aligned with the target role. AI screening probability is moderate to good for junior or developing DevOps/platform roles, but lower for this specific contractor role because the CV does not demonstrate strong Terraform/Terragrunt, cloud environment operation, mTLS, system design, or production infrastructure ownership. The phrase "Terraform (personal project)" is truthful and useful, but it also clearly signals that Terraform experience is limited. ATS parsing would be improved slightly by using a conventional LinkedIn or GitLab URL format and by avoiding the arrow-style career framing in the source title if that version is used elsewhere.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: The CV aligns well with hands-on CI/CD, Kubernetes-based environment automation, Linux, observability, analytical problem-solving, documentation, and ownership of shared engineering workflows. It also supports the company's ownership and engineering-led culture through evidence of owning pipelines, building reusable tooling, documenting systems, and mentoring colleagues. The candidate's strongest directly relevant evidence is the merge-request environment project, GitOps homelab, TLS certificate management, monitoring stack, and quantified pipeline improvements. However, the candidate's material shows genuine gaps against several central requirements: strong Terraform and Terragrunt; substantial cloud environment design and operation; mTLS; production infrastructure ownership; IoT, automotive, or remote-device integration; and backend/full-stack experience. The document should not imply that the candidate operates the Kubernetes cluster or has production cloud/on-call ownership: it correctly states that the platform team operates the cluster. AWS is present only at a basic learning level, while Linux is supported. The profile is therefore a credible developing or junior-to-mid DevOps/platform profile, but not yet a strong match for a contractor expected to shape fleet-connectivity architecture from the start.
critique.improvement_instructions:
CRITICAL / HIGH-VALUE IMPROVEMENTS
1. In the Professional Summary, replace the final sentence "Moving toward a full-time DevOps / platform engineering role" with a more role-relevant but still truthful statement such as: "Building toward a DevOps / platform engineering role focused on CI/CD, infrastructure automation, Kubernetes-based environments, observability, and developer tooling." This removes the job-search framing and foregrounds the capabilities most relevant to Corvale.

2. In the Professional Summary, explicitly qualify the infrastructure scope so the CV remains precise while improving alignment. For example, change "Brings practical infrastructure-as-code experience from a personal Terraform project" to "Brings practical infrastructure-as-code experience from a personal Terraform project, alongside hands-on automation of Kubernetes-based test environments through Helm and GitLab CI." This connects Terraform to the stronger professional infrastructure evidence without overstating Terraform depth.

3. In the Technical Skills section, change the heading "Networking & security: Traefik ingress, cert-manager TLS" to "Networking & TLS: Traefik ingress, cert-manager, SSL/TLS certificate management." The candidate's material supports TLS and certificate management, but not mTLS; do not add mTLS or imply mutual authentication.

4. In the Technical Skills section, revise "Cloud learning: AWS EC2 and S3 basics; Hetzner VPS" to "Cloud and infrastructure learning: AWS EC2 and S3 basics; Hetzner VPS; Terraform provisioning." This more clearly communicates the level and context of cloud experience while connecting it to the infrastructure project.

5. In the Professional Experience section under Odrava Health Software, add the stakeholder outcome supported by the original portfolio to the ephemeral-environment bullet. For example, append: "QA and product teams used the environments to review features before merge, with end-to-end tests running against each environment." This directly demonstrates support for developers and stakeholders and better supports the requirement to bring stakeholders along.

6. In the same Odrava Health section, strengthen the documentation/technical-leadership bullet without overstating formal leadership. Change "Wrote the internal guide to how CI works, which is used in team onboarding; mentored two QA interns in 2023" to: "Authored the internal 'How CI Works' guide used for team onboarding and mentored two QA interns in 2023." This is more concise and gives the documentation contribution a clearer ownership verb.

7. In the Selected Infrastructure Projects section, avoid duplicating the full details of the Merge-Request Ephemeral Environments and CI Pipeline Speed-up projects already covered under Odrava Health. Either remove those two project entries or reduce each to a single line that points to the relevant achievement. Use the recovered space to expand the Homelab project with its operational and observability details, for example: "Deployed applications from Git with Argo CD and configured Prometheus, Grafana and Loki dashboards for cluster and application observability." The current content is truthful but repetitive.

8. In the Homelab k3s Cluster with GitOps project, make the infrastructure scope more concrete by changing "Provisioned infrastructure for a small Hetzner VPS with Terraform; used Ansible at a basic level" to "Provisioned a small Hetzner VPS with Terraform and used Ansible for basic configuration tasks." This is clearer and more ATS-readable while preserving the limited scope.

9. In the Professional Experience section under Odrava Health, retain the sentence "the platform team operates the cluster" because it is an important scope clarification. Do not replace it with wording such as "managed Kubernetes" or "operated the cluster," which would overstate the candidate's experience.

MINOR ATS / PRESENTATION IMPROVEMENTS
10. In the contact line, format the portfolio link as a complete URL, such as "https://gitlab.com/mkb-example," rather than "gitlab.com/mkb-example," to improve parser recognition.

11. In the Certifications & Professional Development section, keep "Certified Kubernetes Administrator (CKA) preparation; exam scheduled for January 2027" exactly qualified as preparation. Do not label it as a certification or "CKA certified" because the original information says the exam has not yet been passed.

critique.content_quality_feedback: This is a strong, truthful transition CV with clear structure, credible metrics, and well-presented CI/CD, Kubernetes test-environment, automation, and observability experience. The quantified pipeline improvement, cost reduction, flaky-test reduction, team scope, and onboarding documentation create convincing evidence of ownership and analytical ability. The main content weakness is that the CV presents several infrastructure projects but does not clearly distinguish professional infrastructure experience from personal learning. The selected-projects section also repeats information already given in the Odrava experience section, reducing space and impact. The headline 'Cloud Infrastructure / DevOps Engineer' is somewhat stronger than the documented level of cloud and production infrastructure ownership, although the summary appropriately adds context.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: The CV is ATS-friendly overall: it uses standard section headings, plain text formatting, chronological experience, recognizable technology names, and job-relevant terms such as Terraform, Kubernetes, Helm, GitLab CI, Docker, Linux, AWS, SSL/TLS, certificate management, observability, and infrastructure as code. Parsing and keyword coverage should be good for adjacent DevOps or platform-engineering screening. AI screening probability is moderate to good for a junior/mid DevOps or platform role, but lower for this specific contractor role because the document does not demonstrate Terragrunt, mTLS, production cloud ownership, system design, or technical security work. The absence of Terragrunt should not be remedied by adding it, because the original candidate information does not support that experience. The duplicated 'See Odrava Health experience' project entries are less useful to ATS and human readers than distinct project descriptions.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: The CV aligns well with the role's infrastructure automation, CI/CD, Kubernetes-based environments, Linux, observability, stakeholder enablement, analytical thinking, and communication themes. It shows relevant hands-on work building ephemeral environments and a personal Terraform-provisioned Hetzner setup, while accurately disclosing namespace-level Kubernetes access and platform-team ownership. It also shows basic AWS exposure through EC2 and S3. The candidate has credible evidence of leading technical topics through ownership of shared pipelines, documentation, mentoring, and workflows used by three product teams. However, the role is seeking a stronger infrastructure engineer who can design and operate cloud environments, maintain Terraform with Terragrunt, contribute to system design, secure train-to-cloud communication using mTLS, and lead infrastructure decisions into production. The candidate's material shows gaps in strong Terraform/Terragrunt, mTLS, explicit system architecture, practical security ownership, IoT or remote-device integration, and backend/full-stack experience. These are candidate-experience gaps rather than document defects and should not be implied or invented in the CV.
critique.improvement_instructions:
1. In the Professional Summary, replace the final sentence 'Building toward a DevOps / platform engineering role focused on CI/CD, infrastructure automation, Kubernetes-based environments, observability, and developer tooling.' with a more evidence-led statement that foregrounds the strongest match: 'Targeting a junior-to-mid DevOps or platform engineering role, with hands-on experience owning CI/CD for three product teams, automating Kubernetes-based ephemeral environments, and building observability and developer tooling.' This is more direct and better calibrated to the documented experience.

2. In the Professional Summary, make the boundary between professional and personal infrastructure experience even clearer by changing 'Brings practical infrastructure-as-code experience from a personal Terraform project, alongside hands-on automation...' to 'Brings personal infrastructure-as-code experience using Terraform on Hetzner, alongside professional hands-on automation of Kubernetes-based test environments using Helm and GitLab CI.' This prevents recruiters from interpreting Terraform as production experience.

3. In the Technical Skills section, change 'Cloud and infrastructure learning: AWS EC2 and S3 basics; Hetzner VPS; Terraform provisioning' to 'Cloud and infrastructure: Terraform provisioning on a personal Hetzner VPS; AWS EC2 and S3 basics from learning projects.' This uses supported details while making the experience level and context immediately clear.

4. In the Selected Infrastructure Projects section, remove the two entries titled 'Merge-Request Ephemeral Environments' and 'CI Pipeline Speed-up' because they only say 'See Odrava Health experience' and duplicate the detailed bullets above. Replace them with the supported 'Flaky Test Dashboard (Odrava Health, 2023)' project, using: 'Collected CI test results through the GitLab API into PostgreSQL and built Grafana dashboards showing flaky tests by team; flaky-test rate fell from 7% to below 1% after teams addressed the highest-frequency failures.' This improves content density and adds an observability/data point relevant to the role.

5. In the Odrava Health experience section, revise the first bullet to include the document's strongest leadership and stakeholder evidence: 'Own GitLab CI pipelines for three product teams (~25 developers), covering build, unit, integration, and end-to-end test stages and artifact publishing; document the workflow for onboarding and coordinate shared engineering practices across QA and product teams.' Use this only if the coordination wording accurately reflects the candidate's existing team interactions; otherwise retain the current wording and add only the documented onboarding-guide clause.

6. In the Homelab project, make the infrastructure and networking scope more ATS-readable by changing the second bullet to: 'Configured Prometheus, Grafana, and Loki for cluster and application observability; configured Traefik ingress and cert-manager for SSL/TLS certificate management.' This preserves the supported experience and explicitly uses the job ad's SSL/TLS terminology without claiming unsupported mTLS.

7. Check the experience dates and the '7 years of experience' statement for consistency. The document lists experience from 2018 to Present; if the CV is being submitted in 2026, update the summary to the accurate total, or use the less date-sensitive wording 'more than seven years of experience.' Do not leave an apparently stale total beside current dates.

8. In the headline, consider changing 'Cloud Infrastructure / DevOps Engineer' to 'QA Automation Engineer | DevOps & Test Infrastructure' or 'DevOps / Platform Engineering Candidate' if the goal is strict calibration to the documented experience. This retains target-role keywords while avoiding an impression of established production cloud-infrastructure ownership.

content:
MARTA KOWAL-BRANDT
QA Automation Engineer (Test Infrastructure)
Wroclaw, Poland | marta.kowalbrandt@example.com | +48 555 303 303 | https://gitlab.com/mkb-example

PROFESSIONAL SUMMARY
QA automation engineer specialising in CI/CD and test infrastructure with 7 years of experience, including ownership of CI/CD pipelines and developer tooling for three product teams (~25 developers). Reduced average pipeline duration from 38 to 14 minutes and monthly CI runner costs by about 30%, while building Kubernetes-based ephemeral test environments with Helm and GitLab CI. Brings namespace-level Kubernetes experience on a shared cluster, plus practical infrastructure-as-code experience from a personal Terraform project and hands-on experience with Docker, Linux, and monitoring. Known for taking ownership of shared engineering workflows and documenting them for team onboarding. Targeting cloud infrastructure and DevOps roles focused on CI/CD, infrastructure automation, Kubernetes-based environments, observability, SSL/TLS certificate management, and developer tooling.

TECHNICAL SKILLS
Infrastructure & CI/CD: Terraform (personal project), GitLab CI, Jenkins, Docker, Docker Compose, Helm, Argo CD
Containers & Linux: Kubernetes (namespace-level experience), k3s, Linux
Monitoring & data: Prometheus, Grafana, Loki, PostgreSQL
Networking & TLS: Traefik ingress, cert-manager, SSL/TLS certificate management (no mTLS experience stated)
Languages & tools: Python, Bash, Java (test code), SQL, Git, Ansible (basic)
Cloud & Infrastructure: Terraform (personal Hetzner VPS project), AWS EC2 and S3 (learning basics), Hetzner VPS, Ansible (basic)
Testing: pytest, Playwright, Selenium, Postman

PROFESSIONAL EXPERIENCE

QA Automation Engineer (Test Infrastructure) | Odrava Health Software, Wroclaw | 2021–Present
- Own GitLab CI pipeline infrastructure and merge-request test-environment workflows for three product teams (~25 developers), covering build, unit, integration and end-to-end test stages and artifact publishing.
- Reduced average pipeline duration from 38 to 14 minutes by profiling workflows, parallelising test jobs, adding dependency caching, and separating end-to-end tests into their own stage; monthly CI runner costs fell by about 30%.
- Built short-lived merge-request environments for applications, PostgreSQL and seeded data, deploying with Helm to the shared Kubernetes cluster from GitLab CI. Environments are automatically removed after merge or 48 hours of inactivity. End-to-end tests run against each environment.
- Maintain a pytest and Playwright end-to-end suite of about 900 tests; reduced the flaky-test rate from 7% to below 1%.
- Wrote Bash and Python tooling to seed PostgreSQL test data and built a Python/GitLab API workflow that collected CI test results into PostgreSQL for Grafana dashboards.
- Authored the internal 'How CI Works' guide used for team onboarding and mentored two QA interns in 2023.
- Work with namespace-level access on the shared Kubernetes cluster; the platform team operates the cluster.

QA Engineer | Brightmill Software House, Wroclaw | 2019–2021
- Tested web and mobile applications for client projects through manual and automated testing.
- Introduced a Java and Selenium automated regression suite for the largest client project.
- Configured Jenkins jobs to run nightly regression tests.

Customer Support Specialist (2nd line) | Brightmill Software House | 2018–2019
- Investigated customer issues using logs and databases, and reproduced bugs for developers.

SELECTED INFRASTRUCTURE PROJECTS

Homelab k3s Cluster with GitOps | Personal | 2024–2025
- Provisioned a small Hetzner VPS with Terraform and used Ansible for basic configuration; deployed applications to a three-node k3s cluster with Argo CD; configured Traefik ingress and cert-manager for SSL/TLS certificates, plus Prometheus, Grafana and Loki for observability.

Flaky Test Dashboard | Odrava Health | 2023
- Collected test results from CI into PostgreSQL and built Grafana dashboards showing flaky tests per team; the flaky rate fell from 7% to below 1% after teams started fixing the top offenders.

EDUCATION
BEng Computer Engineering | Silesian Lowlands University of Technology | 2018

CERTIFICATIONS & PROFESSIONAL DEVELOPMENT
ISTQB Foundation Level | 2019
Certified Kubernetes Administrator (CKA) preparation — exam scheduled for January 2027 (not yet certified)

LANGUAGES
Polish (native) | English (C1) | German (A2)

critique.content_quality_feedback: This is a strong, credible and well-structured CV with clear progression from QA automation into test infrastructure and DevOps-oriented work. The quantified achievements are particularly effective: pipeline duration reduced from 38 to 14 minutes, runner costs reduced by about 30%, and flaky tests reduced from 7% to below 1%. The experience bullets explain both the technical work and its business or team impact. The CV is also appropriately transparent about namespace-level Kubernetes access, personal Terraform usage, AWS learning, and the CKA exam not yet being completed. The main content weakness is that the document sometimes reads as a highly qualified QA/test-infrastructure profile rather than a direct cloud infrastructure engineer profile. This is largely due to the candidate's actual experience rather than poor writing. The parenthetical statement about no mTLS experience is unnecessarily defensive and should be removed from the CV.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: The CV uses ATS-friendly standard headings, chronological experience, plain text formatting, recognizable technology names, and measurable achievements. It should parse well and has a high AI-screening probability for QA automation, CI/CD, test infrastructure, Kubernetes test environments, and junior-to-mid DevOps roles. For this particular vacancy, screening probability is moderate because Terraform is explicitly limited to a personal project, Terragrunt is absent, mTLS is not demonstrated, and AWS is only at learning level. The Skills section contains useful keywords such as Terraform, GitLab CI, Kubernetes, Helm, Docker, Linux, Prometheus, Grafana, SSL/TLS, Python, Bash, and AWS EC2/S3. However, Terraform and Ansible are repeated across multiple skill categories, while the distinction between professional, personal, and learning experience could be made more consistent. There are no obvious parsing problems such as tables, graphics, columns, icons, or unusual section names.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: The CV aligns well with the role's infrastructure engineering, CI/CD, Kubernetes-based environment operation, observability, Linux, SSL/TLS certificate management, analytical thinking, documentation, ownership, and technical communication themes. It also provides credible evidence of leading a technical topic across three product teams and bringing teams along through onboarding documentation and mentoring. The candidate's experience with Helm, cert-manager, Traefik, Prometheus, Grafana, Loki, GitLab CI, and short-lived environments is relevant to Corvale's emphasis on secure, observable and maintainable platforms. The principal requirement gaps are strong Terraform and Terragrunt, mTLS, broader cloud environment design and operation, explicit practical security work, and IoT or remote-device integration. AWS is present only as learning basics, and no virtual-machine experience is documented. The Java experience is relevant as JVM-based test automation, but the material does not show backend or full-stack development. These are candidate-experience gaps, not defects that can be solved by rewriting the CV.
critique.improvement_instructions:
MINOR ENHANCEMENTS:
1. In the Professional Summary, remove the parenthetical phrase "(no mTLS experience stated)" from the Skills section and do not replace it with an mTLS claim. Negative disclaimers are not useful ATS keywords and make the document sound defensive. Retain the truthful SSL/TLS and cert-manager experience.
2. In the Professional Summary, make the leadership and cross-team scope slightly more explicit by changing "with ownership of CI/CD pipelines and developer tooling for three product teams (~25 developers)" to "owning CI/CD pipeline infrastructure and developer tooling for three product teams (~25 developers), and leading improvements adopted across those teams." This is supported by the documented ownership, pipeline optimization, onboarding guide, and team usage.
3. In the Odrava Health Software experience section, revise the first bullet to foreground technical leadership without overstating authority: "Own CI/CD pipeline infrastructure and merge-request test-environment workflows for three product teams (~25 developers), coordinating build, unit, integration and end-to-end test stages and artifact publishing." This better matches the advertisement's language about leading technical topics and supporting multiple teams.
4. In the Technical Skills section, consolidate the repeated Terraform and Ansible entries. For example, use one line such as "Infrastructure as Code: Terraform (personal Hetzner VPS project), Ansible (basic)" and retain a separate "Cloud: AWS EC2 and S3 (learning basics), Hetzner VPS." This improves scanability and prevents the skills section from appearing padded.
5. In the Homelab k3s Cluster with GitOps project, clarify the infrastructure scope so recruiters do not infer production-cluster ownership: change the first bullet to "Provisioned a small Hetzner VPS with Terraform and basic Ansible configuration; deployed applications to a three-node Raspberry Pi 5 k3s cluster with Argo CD." This more precisely reflects the candidate portfolio information.
6. In the Professional Summary, consider changing "Targeting cloud infrastructure and DevOps roles focused on..." to a role-specific capability statement such as "Focuses on CI/CD, infrastructure automation, Kubernetes-based environments, observability, SSL/TLS certificate management, and developer tooling." This removes aspirational wording and gives the section a more confident, evidence-based tone.
